text: The first real build: the Partner Warranty Claims scoped application, and the Warranty Claim table inside it.
x_brind_claims gets created in Studio, then the x_brind_claims_warranty_claim table, built without extending Task so its five states stay exactly what Brindlewood needs.
All seven fields go in as designed: partner_company as a reference to Company, state as a five-value choice, labor_hours and parts_cost sized correctly.
Nothing guards this data yet. No ACL, no portal, no automation, no API -- just a real table with real fields.
Next: turning the planned access rule into an actual enforced ACL.
